alt.en: An old printed music page numbered 12, headed "Nôs Calan" and "No. 7", marked Moderato, with the tune and bass on paired staves in G and three variations below, marked "Var: 1st", "Var: 2d" and "Var: 3d".
alt.es: Página de música impresa antigua con el número 12, con los encabezados "Nôs Calan" y "No. 7", marcada Moderato, con la melodía y el bajo en pentagramas emparejados en Sol y tres variaciones debajo, marcadas "Var: 1st", "Var: 2d" y "Var: 3d".

caption.en: "Nôs Calan", No. 7 in the harper John Parry's British Harmony (Ruabon and London, 1781), in G with three variations: the tune's earliest known printing under that name.
caption.es: "Nôs Calan", n.º 7 de British Harmony, del arpista John Parry (Ruabon y Londres, 1781), en Sol y con tres variaciones: la primera impresión conocida de la melodía con ese nombre.

source: John Parry, British Harmony, being a Collection of Antient Welsh Airs (Ruabon and London, 1781), p. 12, No. 7, "Nôs Calan"
callNumber: NLW digital object 4675640 (image 4675658, p. 12); handle http://hdl.handle.net/10107/4675640
licenceEvidence: NLW IIIF manifest https://iiif.llyfrgell.cymru/manifests/2.0/4675640/manifest.json: "license": "http://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/", "attribution": "Llyfrgell Genedlaethol Cymru – The National Library of Wales". Printed 1781; Parry died 1782.
credit: Llyfrgell Genedlaethol Cymru – The National Library of Wales

alt.en: A tall wooden harp standing on a plain grey ground, its reddish-brown frame painted with small gold patterns, with many strings running from the curved neck down to the long soundbox.
alt.es: Un arpa alta de madera sobre un fondo gris liso, con el marco marrón rojizo pintado con pequeños motivos dorados y muchas cuerdas que bajan del cuello curvo a la larga caja de resonancia.

caption.en: A Welsh triple harp made about 1750 by John Richards of Llanrwst, the leading Welsh harp maker of his century: Nos Galan was a harp air, printed by the harpers John Parry in 1781 and Edward Jones in 1784.
caption.es: Un arpa triple galesa construida hacia 1750 por John Richards, de Llanrwst, el principal constructor de arpas de Gales de su siglo: Nos Galan era una pieza para arpa, impresa por los arpistas John Parry en 1781 y Edward Jones en 1784.

source: Welsh Triple Harp, John Richards (Llanrwst, 1711-1789), ca. 1750, wood and various materials, height 198.5 cm
library: The Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York

alt.en: A printed songbook page numbered 325, headed "The Song Book", "CCXLVIII" and "Deck the Hall with Boughs of Holly", with the tune on one staff over the first verse, the second and third verses below, and the note "Words (translated from Talhaiarn) by Oliphant. Tune New Year's Eve. From Thomas's Welsh Melodies."
alt.es: Página impresa de un cancionero con el número 325, con los encabezados "The Song Book", "CCXLVIII" y "Deck the Hall with Boughs of Holly", con la melodía en un pentagrama sobre la primera estrofa, la segunda y la tercera debajo, y la nota "Words (translated from Talhaiarn) by Oliphant. Tune New Year's Eve. From Thomas's Welsh Melodies."

caption.en: Thomas Oliphant's words in John Hullah's The Song Book (1866), with "Fill the mead-cup, drain the barrel" in the first verse and the credit "translated from Talhaiarn", which the Welsh words do not bear out.
caption.es: La letra de Thomas Oliphant en The Song Book de John Hullah (1866), con "Fill the mead-cup, drain the barrel" en la primera estrofa y la atribución "translated from Talhaiarn" (traducido de Talhaiarn), que la letra galesa no confirma.

source: John Hullah, The Song Book: Words and Tunes from the Best Poets and Musicians (London: Macmillan; Philadelphia: J. B. Lippincott, 1866), No. CCXLVIII, p. 325, "Deck the Hall with Boughs of Holly"
library: Princeton Theological Seminary Library (digitized by the Internet Archive)
licenceEvidence: Published 1866; Hullah died 1884, Oliphant 1873, Talhaiarn 1869, John Thomas 1913. US: published before 1931. EU and Israel: life plus 70 ended 1983 at the latest. Faithful scan of a flat page (see rights.md).
credit: Princeton Theological Seminary Library, via the Internet Archive

alt.en: A black-and-white journal page numbered 226, headed "Pennsylvania School Journal" and "Dec.", with two columns of text on "The Twelve Intervals" above "Deck the Hall with Boughs of Holly", marked "Welsh Air", in four parts on two staves with three verses between them.
alt.es: Página de revista en blanco y negro con el número 226, con los encabezados "Pennsylvania School Journal" y "Dec.", con dos columnas de texto sobre "The Twelve Intervals" encima de "Deck the Hall with Boughs of Holly", marcada "Welsh Air", a cuatro voces en dos pentagramas y con tres estrofas entre ellos.

caption.en: The Pennsylvania School Journal of December 1877 printed the carol in four parts as a "Welsh Air", with "Don we now our gay apparel" where Oliphant had the mead-cup: the American words most people sing.
caption.es: El Pennsylvania School Journal de diciembre de 1877 imprimió el villancico a cuatro voces como "Welsh Air" (aire galés), con "Don we now our gay apparel" donde Oliphant tenía la copa de hidromiel: la letra estadounidense que canta casi todo el mundo.

source: The Pennsylvania School Journal, vol. 26, no. 6 (December 1877), p. 226, "Deck the Hall with Boughs of Holly" (cropped to the page head and the carol)
licenceEvidence: Published December 1877 by the Pennsylvania State Education Association; the carol's reviser and arranger are unnamed (anonymous, 70 years from publication, ended 1947); if the reviser was the journal's editor J. P. McCaskey, he died 1935 (life plus 70 ended 2005). US: published before 1931. Faithful scan of a flat page (see rights.md).
